predecessors.name: Sunda Kingdom
predecessors.text: Banten, the western port province of the Sunda Kingdom; the infobox lists the Sunda Kingdom, the Cirebon Sultanate and the Demak Sultanate as predecessors

predecessors.name: Sultanate of Cirebon
predecessors.text: Old Banten, a province of Cirebon after 1531

successors.name: Dutch East Indies
successors.text: Banten, absorbed into the Dutch East Indies: 'The Sultanate of Banten had been absorbed into the territory of the Dutch East Indies', declared Daendels on 22 November 1808 in Serang

ledger.x: 1526: Syarif Hidayatullah conquers Banten from the Sunda Kingdom.
1552: Banten becomes independent of Cirebon under Hasanuddin.
1572: Banten holds the west of the old Sunda lands.
1576: Banten's pressure on the Sunda Kingdom turns into the final campaign.
1579: Banten razes Pakuan and the Sunda Kingdom ends.
1619: the Dutch storm Jayakarta and found Batavia.
1661: Banten extends its authority to Landak in western Borneo.
1677: Ageng Tirtayasa makes himself master of Cirebon.
1683: the VOC takes Bogor and the Priangan highlands and Banten becomes its client.
1683: Banten's predominance over Cirebon ends with Ageng's surrender.
1683: Ageng Tirtayasa surrenders to the VOC.
1752: the Dutch annex Banten's lands in southern Sumatra.
1752: the Dutch annex 'territories on western Borneo', which this dossier reads as including Landak.
1808: Daendels abolishes the Sultanate of Banten.

wars.name: Banten's conquest of the Sunda Kingdom
wars.outcome: Pakuan razed in 1579; the Sunda Kingdom ends and Banten 'took over most of the former Sunda Kingdom's territory'.

wars.name: Banten-VOC conflict over Jayakarta and the pepper trade
wars.outcome: Jayakarta lost in 1619; a blockade of Banten harbour for about 15 years; a 1639 treaty forced Banten to recognise Batavia.

wars.name: Revolts of Bengkulu and Lampung
wars.outcome: 'Bengkulu rebelled in 1640 while Lampung rebelled in 1641 and 1644.'

wars.name: Pagarage (Pacirebonan) war
wars.outcome: A Banten victory over Cirebon-Mataram forces.

wars.name: Banten civil war and VOC intervention
wars.outcome: Haji, backed by the VOC, defeated his father Ageng Tirtayasa, who surrendered in March 1683; Banten became a VOC client state and the VOC gained Bogor and the Priangan highlands.

certainty.note: No survey or treaty line anywhere: the Sumatran claim to 1752 is a sphere of ports and river mouths, and the West Java frontier moves with Mataram, Cirebon and the VOC without a dated line.
